name: Amri Karbi

catalog_quote: Stress in Amri Karbi is predictable. Therefore, we assume that there is no stress in the underlining form of a word. However, the surface form has stress. So, the following stress pattern for Amri Karbi can be proposed: Amri Karbi stress parse into binary-syllabic feet, i.e. each foot has two syllables, starting at the right-most edge of the word. Amri Karbi has both primary and secondary stress. Feet in Amri Karbi are right-headed, i.e. iambic. The primary stress resigns on the first foot at the foot head position and the secondary stress falls on the head of the second foot. Stress in Amri Karbi is not contrastive; however, it interacts with the surface realization of tone (see more in §2.4.3). ... tone_statements.citation: Philippova, Nailya. 2025. Negation in Amri Karbi. In Matti Miestamo & Ljuba Veselinova (eds.), Negation in the world's languages II: Eurasia (Chapter 12), 345-378. Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.18233972
tone_statements.quote: Amri Karbi is a tonal language, with three tones, low, medium and high, which exhibit low functional load. In the text examples tone is marked only on those items where the tone category was identified. Since there is a high variability and fluctuation of tone, only underlying tone is marked in the text examples. Tone in the text examples is marked by diacritics, e.g. á ‘High’, à ‘Low’, ā ‘Mid’.

audit.reasoning: The classification (predictable, non-contrastive final primary stress; right-to-left iambic feet; secondary on head of second foot; domain = phonological word; clitics and -po/-pe/-so unstressed) rests on the best and only reference grammar of the language (Philippova 2021, 468 pp incl. front matter), which we hold as the open-access Helsinki PDF; every quoted passage and locator (§2.4.1 pp.45-46 exx. 2.6-2.8, p.27, §3 pp.61-62, §2.4.3 p.51) was confirmed verbatim in the text we hold. The Glottolog bibliography offers nothing stronger: the one other item is an unpublished 2012 wordlist-based conference phonology that Philippova herself reviews and supersedes. The one open item found and downloaded today (Teronpi 2025, Ri-Bhoi variety, 8 pp) treats segments only and is explicitly silent on prosody, so it neither confirms nor challenges the record. no reclassification or re-read is indicated.

Segmental inventory (21 C, 7 V) from an 835-word list in Umrang village, Ri-Bhoi (Meghalaya); 'suprasegmental phonemes include the tone system' but the paper states it 'fails to perform a thorough examination of many important features such as the prosodic or suprasegmental features due to time constraint' (p.46).

sources.note: Section 1 'The language' restates the author's analysis - Amri Karbi is tonal with three tones (low, mid, high) of low functional load; high variability/fluctuation of tone, so only underlying tone is marked (diacritics) on items whose tone category was identified. No further tone analysis; consistent with the statement listed here (Philippova 2021 sec. 2.4.2).

sources.note: Only other Glottolog descriptive item for amri1238; a phonetician-authored phonology sketch (Sonapur variety) that may contain an independent statement on stress/tone to cross-check Philippova's iambic-final analysis.
